passages.t: ‘If the LORD had not been on our side’, and the bird out of the snare
passages.happening:
The heading reads, “A song of ascents. Of David” (verse 1). A leader calls the people to join in. “If the LORD had not been on our side” (verse 1), and then, “let Israel now declare” it with him (verse 1). The line is repeated: “if the LORD had not been on our side when men attacked us” (verse 2).

Then the psalm imagines what would have happened, with ‘then’ again and again: “then they would have swallowed us alive” (verse 3), “then the floods would have engulfed us, then the torrent would have overwhelmed us” (verse 4), “then the raging waters would have swept us away” (verse 5).

But it did not happen. “Blessed be the LORD, who has not given us as prey to their teeth” (verse 6). “We have escaped like a bird from the snare of the fowler; the net is torn, and we have slipped away” (verse 7). The psalm ends, “Our help is in the name of the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth” (verse 8).
passages.hearers:
This is a song for a crowd. A leader sings the first line, and the people repeat it. It looks back on a narrow escape. The psalm does not say which one. Some think of a particular rescue, others of the return from exile, and many think it was written so that any rescue could be remembered with it. The note on Psalm 120 explains the Songs of Ascents.

The pictures are strong. Being ‘swallowed alive’ recalls the ground opening in the desert under Korah and those with him (Numbers 16:30-33). The floods recall the dry stream beds of the land, which can fill without warning after rain and sweep away anything in them. Rushing water was also an old picture of chaos and death.

A fowler was a man who caught birds with nets and snares. A bird in a snare cannot free itself. It gets away only if the snare breaks. That is the point of verse 7. ‘The net is torn’, and the people did not tear it. God did.

Verse 8 is the same answer Psalm 121 gave to its question: help comes from the Maker of heaven and earth.
passages.later:
Proverbs uses the same picture: “Free yourself, like a gazelle from the hand of the hunter, like a bird from the snare of the fowler” (Proverbs 6:5).

Paul asked, “If God is for us, who can be against us?” (Romans 8:31). He also looked back on a time near death and said, “He has delivered us from such a deadly peril, and He will deliver us” (2 Corinthians 1:10).
passages.asks:
‘If the LORD had not been on our side.’ Try finishing that sentence about your own life. Where would you be? Most people can name at least one moment when the net tore.

Remembering is part of faith. Psalm 124 teaches God's people to say aloud, together, what he has done, so that the next generation will know it too.
